neet_che_u04_t06_1.working: By convention, ΔfH° = 0 only for an element in its most stable standard state. Graphite, O2(g) and Br2(l) are the reference forms. Diamond is not the reference form of carbon, so its ΔfH° (about +1.9 kJ/mol) is not zero.

neet_che_u04_t06_2.working: ΔrH = Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed) = (436 + 242) − 2(431) = 678 − 862 = −184 kJ.

neet_che_u04_t06_3.working: Atomizing CH4 breaks four C-H bonds, so the average C-H bond enthalpy = 1664/4 = 416 kJ/mol.

neet_che_u04_t06_4.working: ΔsolH = ΔlatticeH + ΔhydH. For NH4Cl the lattice enthalpy outweighs the magnitude of the hydration enthalpy, so ΔsolH is positive. Dissolution is therefore endothermic, and R correctly explains A.

neet_che_u04_t06_5.working: Statement I is false because hydration enthalpy is negative. Statement II is false because ΔsubH = ΔfusH + ΔvapH, so ΔsubH is greater than ΔvapH.
